text: Nine A.M. Board meeting. And the deck doesn't match the model.
You ask a chatbot to update the board memo.
It says it's done.
Then you open the file... and the formatting's wrecked.
So you fix it by hand. Then, an email.
Please update the model and the board deck to match, before the meeting.
So you ask it for the deck... and it builds one, in the chat.
But the deck... still has the old number.
Prompt again. Wait again. Five minutes... for one number.
Done. Except now... slide four changed.
Five tabs. Copy. Paste. Check. Repeat.
The worst part? You don't even know what's wrong anymore.
See exactly what changed. Decide what stays.
Not another chatbot. Your workspace: Word, Excel and PowerPoint, together.
Start from your templates, or just describe it.
Tell it what changed, once. It finds where that number lives: the model, the memo, the deck.
It plans the work, then checks it. And the number it validated travels with it.
No regenerating. It edits the cell, the sentence, the slide element, and leaves the rest alone.
Every change is marked, in every file. Accept it, or reject it. Even slide four.
Bring in your team. People, and their assistants, on the same files.
You see each proposal, and you decide what lands.
Each answer shows its sources, file by file, so you can check before you trust.
Your workspace. Your files, stored on your device.
Done. And this time, you've seen every change.
Agentic Office.
